relative_flux.required_relative_character: If matter has intrinsic line chi, relative flux must transform in chi^-1, and additional gauge representations must contract to a true singlet.
relative_flux.important: This is a NONZERO absolute H1 × relative H2 -> relative H3 topological pairing (flux-induced bilinear), not an ordinary 1+1+1 bulk Yukawa. Flux values, quantization, gauge representations, Higgs vevs, and spinor index/physical mass generation are not derived. Relative flux cannot automatically mass up unpaired chiral fermions without a gauge-appropriate conjugate field.

SU5_covariant_octet_spurion.gauge_invariant_candidate: Tr[ P8(24F;24H) P8(24F;24H) ] is SU5 invariant if 24H -> U 24H U† jointly with 24F, evaluated around vev diag(2,2,2,-3,-3)*v
SU5_covariant_octet_spurion.operator_hierarchy: P8 polynomial in H/v through H². Its quadratic mass term has operators up to (24H/v)^4 (24F)^2. The v factors are inserted/unknown; heavy UV origin, supersymmetric holomorphic contractions, nonrenormalizable coefficients and lower-order counterterms need derivation.
SU5_covariant_octet_spurion.correction_to_prior: Frozen H projector not SU5 invariant under transforming F alone, but covariant as an adjoint-Higgs spurion. An explicit SU5-breaking boundary is not the ONLY mathematical way to select an octet; the physical higher-dimensional origin and tunings remain open.

causal_mass_counterterm.exact_theorem: For local KG mass term B_mu[f]=B[f]+mu² f(origin) with fixed f(origin), shift is deterministic: Var(B_mu)=Var(B) exactly.
causal_mass_counterterm.mass_from_bias_is_regulator_dependent: The mass-squared counterterm needed to erase the finite-volume constant bias changes sign between rho100 eps.2 and rho200 eps.2, so it cannot be a universal positive physical particle rest mass.
causal_mass_counterterm.scope: Future cone constant probe in flat Minkowski, numeric Poisson variance, analytic finite-density mean; no quantum state, Einstein operator, canonical propagating scalar or renormalization condition from a microscopic action.
